column1: # tlstore items — hand-maintained. build-catalog.sh adds the digests and the
# serial and writes dist/catalog.tsv; never edit that file.
# Tab separated, the catalog's columns minus the digest, picture-digest,
# readme-digest and demo-digest columns (all computed by build-catalog.sh):
#   name  kind  version  prefixes  source  target  requires  options  summary
#   category  upstream  setup  standfirst  does1  does2  does3  try  notes
#   author  licence  size  picture  demo  featured  readme-skip  readme
# kind      pkg
column9: bundle

column1: #           (archive: an app that is a whole directory, one .tar.gz whose top
#           level is the app's root, unpacked into ~/.local/lib/<name> and
#           replaced whole on update; needs exe=. docs/SPEC.md, Revision 14)
#           (skill: an agent skill, one .tar.gz whose only top-level entry is
#           a folder named like the item, unpacked into ~/.agents/skills/<name>,
#           replaced whole on update, and linked from ~/.claude/skills/<name>
#           and, while ~/.codex is there, ~/.codex/skills/<name>. No wrapper.
#           docs/SPEC.md, Revision 18)
# version   - for pkg, bundle and fisher; the upstream version for a binary or an
#           archive (<upstream>+<commit>.<N> when build.yml builds it, so a
#           rebuild moves it); the launcher tag or commit for a template or a
#           skill; latest or a pin for npm-musl and npm-android
# prefixes  * or a comma list of app packages; one row per (name, prefix set),
#           so the per-edition builds are two rows sharing a name
# source    pkg: package names. binary/archive/skill/file: launcher:<path>@<tag or
#           commit>, binaries:<asset>@<tag>, or a URL. npm-musl/npm-android:
#           npm:<package>#<exe>.
#           fisher: the plugin list, space separated
# target    where it lands, ~ allowed; - means the default (an archive: the
#           directory ~/.local/lib/<name>; a skill: the directory
#           ~/.agents/skills/<name>, the links being named after the item
#           wherever it lands)
# requires  comma list installed first; a bundle's members live here
# options   ;-separated key=value: env=K=V (comma repeats), tz=1, mode=755,
#           build=<packages needed only while installing>, hidden=1,
#           retired=1 (this item is gone; update removes it from a phone that
#           already has it, and install refuses it. Always paired with
#           hidden=1 — an older engine, which knows nothing of retired=1,
#           must still see only a hidden part it never offers or installs.
#           The row keeps its real kind/source/target/digest so update can
#           still tell a shipped file from an edited one),
#           musl-libs=<hidden binary items copied in beside the musl loader,
#           for an npm-musl binary that needs more of musl than its libc>,
#           extra=<path,path> (npm-musl and npm-android: more members of the
#           package, paths inside package/, unpacked beside the executable
#           under their package paths and made executable; one missing fails
#           the install like a missing executable),
#           exe=<path> (archive only, required: the program inside the
#           archive the wrapper execs, relative to its top level; it must be
#           there and executable or the install fails),
#           command=<name> (npm-musl, npm-android and archive: the wrapper's
#           name, instead of the executable's basename or the item's name),
#           args=<words> (npm-musl, npm-android and archive: written into the
#           wrapper's exec line before "$@", unquoted, so plain words only;
#           env= and tz=1 go in the same wrapper),
#           host=launcher|termux (comma list; absent means both),
#           min-launcher=X.Y.Z (the oldest launcher that may have it),
#           priv=shizuku (binary only: the launcher runs it as the Shizuku
#           shell user through its privileged lane. The program lands off PATH
#           under ~/.local/lib/tlstore/priv/<name> and a wrapper at
#           ~/.local/bin/<name> hands it to tl-priv, so the row requires
#           tl-priv and is host=launcher; docs/maintainer/catalog.md),
#           conflicts=<pkg,pkg> (packages that own the same commands: install
#           refuses, naming the package to remove, while one of them is
#           installed. Put it on the visible item and on every part, since a
#           part installs first. docs/maintainer/termux-api-shims.md),
#           x86_64:source=<source>, x86_64:target=<path> (the x86_64 build,
#           standing in for source and target on an x86_64 device; the row's
#           own columns are the aarch64 build. An npm-musl/npm-android row is
#           offered on x86_64 only with an x86_64:source. A binary's or an
#           archive's x86_64:digest is never written here: build-catalog.sh
#           appends it when SHA256SUMS has <asset>-x86_64, and without it the
#           item is not offered on x86_64. docs/SPEC.md, Revision 12),
#           login-shell=<shell> (bundle only: after the members are in, chsh -s
#           <shell> makes it the shell new sessions start in; remove takes the
#           ~/.termux/shell link away again while it still points at that shell),
#           pkg-size=<download MB>,<disk MB> (a visible item whose Termux
#           packages, its own and its parts', are large: what they take on a
#           stock Termux, as scripts/pkg-weight.py prints it, never guessed.
#           Over 50 MB of either, its page says so before install and install
#           says so before it asks, when apt cannot say more. docs/SPEC.md,
#           Revision 15),
#           pkg-what=<words> (what those packages are, for that sentence:
#           "Also installs <words>: about …"; default "packages from Termux"),
#           repo=1 (pkg only: its package adds a package source, as x11-repo
#           does. It is installed in a call of its own and the package lists
#           are read again before the rest, which may come from that source;
#           what comes from it requires this item)
# summary   one plain sentence — it is what list and search show the user
# tlstore-ui (Revision 5) reads the rest through `tlstore info --tsv`/`list
# --tsv`; a part (hidden=1) leaves them all "-"/0. Rules for each field:
# docs/REVISION-6.md (Revision 5's item-spread-rules.md is retired by it).
#   category    Note taking | Tools | AI | - (a part, or a setup with none)
#   upstream    owner/repo the program comes from; - for a setup or a part
#   setup       1 for the launcher's own arrangement (fish-shell), else 0
#   standfirst  <=42 chars, lower case, no brand name, no full stop; - if none
#   does1..3    exactly three, each <=40 chars, starting with a verb; - if none
#   try         one safe command to run right after installing; - if none
#   notes       0-2 short facts, "|"-separated; - if none
#   author      who makes it, plainly; - if unknown
#   licence     its licence; - if unknown or (for a setup) not one thing
#   size        only when it can be stated truthfully, e.g. "~200 MB"; - else
#   picture     a launcher: source for its cover picture; - if none exists
#   demo        a launcher: source for a short clip of `try` working; - if none
#   featured    1 for the one item the home screen shows large, else 0
#   readme-skip headings of the upstream README's sections the item page
#               leaves out, "|"-separated (Revision 6); - if none
#   readme      a launcher:/binaries: source for a pinned copy of the item's
#               README, read instead of fetching the upstream one; - to keep
#               fetching upstream (pinned content, Revision 6 addendum).
#               build-catalog.sh computes readme-digest and demo-digest (the
#               digest for `readme` and for `demo`) alongside it the same way
#               it already computes picture-digest for `picture`.
# Thirteen items are visible, in the order they appear here: btop, claude-code,
# codex, dawn, fastfetch, fish-shell, kitten, opencode, herdr, tuios, sigye,
# terminal-browser, termux-api-shims.
# Everything else is
# hidden=1 — a part another item pulls in, never listed and never installed by
# name.
# fastfetch links libandroid-glob and dlopens ImageMagick and Chafa for the
# animated logo, so its libraries are a pkg item it requires rather than a note
# nobody reads.
